reasoning.Student A: Because the mechanism is strategy-proof, truthful reporting of my preferences is a dominant strategy: I cannot improve my assignment by misrepresenting my ranking regardless of what others do. My true preference is w > y > x > z. I have top priority (1) at both w and y and lower priority (2) at x and z. Although many other applicants prefer y > x > w > z (so competition for y may be high), strategy-proofness means I should still list my true order — ranking w first (my favorite) is correct, even if others crowd y. Any attempt to manipulate the order to "game" the mechanism could only leave me the same or worse off, so I submit my true ranking.
reasoning.Student B: Because the mechanism is strategy-proof, my dominant action is to report my true preferences. Misrepresenting cannot improve my assignment regardless of how others rank schools. My true preference ordering is w > y > z > x, so I should submit that order. Although many applicants favor y and x highly, and my priorities are w:2, x:1, y:2, z:1, strategic manipulation would not yield a better guaranteed outcome under a strategy-proof mechanism.
reasoning.Student C: Because the mechanism is strategy-proof, reporting your true preferences is a dominant strategy: no misreport can yield a better assignment regardless of what others do. Although y may be competitive (many applicants prefer y), misrepresenting preferences (e.g., ranking a lower-valued school higher to try to "game" priorities) cannot improve your outcome under a strategy-proof mechanism. Therefore you should rank schools in the true order y > w > z > x.
reasoning.Student D: Because the mechanism is strategy-proof, my dominant strategy is to report my true preferences; I cannot improve my outcome by misrepresenting rankings regardless of how others (who mostly favor y > x > w > z) submit their preferences or the schools' priorities. Although my priority ranks are relatively low (w:4, x:4, y:3, z:3), that does not change the fact that truthful reporting is optimal. Therefore I should and will rank the schools in my true preference order: w > z > y > x.
